items.headline: Logan: Fed needs 'at least two more' 25bp hikes, then a pause — Dallas Fed president puts a number on the tightening path after voting for the Oct 28 hold
Musalem: Fed needs a hike 'again soon' — policy still accommodative, inflation remains elevated; gradual moves preferable
Gold crashes below $3,900 (-3%+, low $3,891) to a one-year low despite a softer dollar and lower yields; Dec Fed hike pricing trimmed to ~70% (from 84% post-FOMC)
US Chicago PMI cools to 55.3 in October (vs 56.0 WSJ poll, prev 58.8) — activity cooling but still expanding; prices paid highest since Dec 2021
German flash CPI cools more than expected — 2.8% y/y (HICP 2.8% vs 3.1% poll, prev 3.3%), core 2.1% (prev 2.4%); relief after hot French/Italian flashes
items.source: Edge Consultancy Oct 30: Germany's provisional October consumer prices — https://edgeconsultancykw.com/italy-inflation-5-4-german-import-prices-10-4-europe-october-2026/

items.headline: US ECI INLINE: Q3 +0.8% q/q as expected (prev 0.9%) — wages +0.7%, benefits +0.9%; labor costs cooling into the December decision; dollar little changed (EUR/USD ~1.1189 post-release)
Canada GDP MISSED: August flat (0.0% vs +0.2% exp, prev 0.0%) — the advance estimate's rebound did not materialize; loonie firmer anyway (USD/CAD ~1.3959) on the oil bid

items.headline: Oil holds the bid Friday morning — Brent ~$116.1, WTI ~$103.4 (intraday $106.2, highest since mid-Sep) on WSJ: CENTCOM chief briefed Trump on Iran options Thu; strikes possible after the Nov 3 midterms; a tanker was struck near Hormuz Thu (UKMTO)
Eurozone Q3 GDP beat (+0.4% q/q vs 0.2% fcst, +1.3% y/y) but France contracted (-0.1%) and Italy flat; EZ jobless up to 6.5% — EUR/USD ~1.1202 after the print, EUR/GBP at a 19-month low ~0.8336
French flash CPI hot (+3.4% y/y vs 3.2% exp, HICP 3.8%) and Italian CPI a sharp beat (+5.4% y/y) while Spanish CPI inline at 4.9% — German flash CPI due 8:00am CT, EZ-wide flash CPI unconfirmed
Gold slips below $4,000 as the dollar stays offered into the US ECI print
Ueda: underlying inflation 'generally consistent' with the 2% target — first such call since 2013; December hike credible, pace data-dependent; USD/JPY dipped to 157.12 then recovered to ~157.5-157.7

Overnight pulse (1:00 AM CT): DXY below 102.00 (~101.85, -0.33%) on AI-led risk-off; EUR/USD ~1.1194, GBP/USD ~1.339, USD/JPY ~157.4 post-BoJ, USD/CHF ~0.8214; Brent ~$116.14, WTI ~$103.43 on Iran-strike reports; gold ~$3,996-4,017; 10Y 4.98%, 2Y ~4.61% — levels are indicative index quotes, not executable prices

items.headline: Oil jumps in Asia — Brent ~$116.14, WTI ~$103.43 — on reports of possible renewed US action on Iran (WSJ: CENTCOM briefed Trump on options Thu); strike-timing claims (Oct 30-31) are single-source and unconfirmed; PBoC sets Oct 30 fixing at 6.7138, a large weak-side gap vs the 6.6548 estimate

items.headline: Japan housing starts swing to a fall in September — down 2.7% y/y (vs +2.5% fcst, prev +6.1%)

BoJ HOLDS at 1.25% (8-1; Takata dissented for 1.50%) — Outlook Report judges underlying inflation 'generally consistent' with the 2% target, FY2027 core CPI median raised to 2.6% (from 2.4%); ETF sales accelerated to ~¥860B/yr from Jan 2027; December hike ~80%; Ueda presser 1:30am CT

items.headline: Dollar slips below 102.00 on AI-led risk-off as yen holds ahead of the BoJ
Australia PPI a touch hot (+1.1% q/q vs 1.0% exp, +3.6% y/y), credit steady (+0.6% m/m vs 0.5% exp, +8.4% y/y) — no new signal before the RBA’s Nov 2-3 meeting
Japan factories beat, shoppers miss — IP +2.2% m/m (vs +1.3% exp, Oct outlook +5.1%) but retail +2.3% y/y (vs 3.3% exp, -0.7% m/m); jobs tighten to 2.4% (ratio 1.19) — mixed read hours before the BoJ
